old: Then, to lift the old king's heart, the eldest of the Kurus, Bhishma,
new: Then, to lift Duryodhana's heart, Bhishma, the eldest of the Kurus and their grandsire,
why: 1.12 tasya samjanayan harsham kuruvriddhah pitamahah: Bhishma cheers 'him', Duryodhana, who has just spoken; 'the old king' points to Dhritarashtra, who is not on the field. Arnold's 'aged king' is his own slip.

old: On the sacred plain of Kurukshetra, drawn up and hungry for battle — tell me, Sanjaya: what did my people do, and what did the sons of Pandu do?
new: On the sacred plain of Kurukshetra my people and the sons of Pandu have gathered, hungry for battle. Tell me, Sanjaya: what did they do?
why: 1.1 samaveta yuyutsavah mamakah pandavas caiva: the participles dangle with no subject until the end; the poem's first line trips aloud.

old: ready to do the bidding in war of the wicked-minded son of Dhritarashtra
new: ready in this war to please the wicked-minded son of Dhritarashtra
why: 1.23 yuddhe priyacikirshavah, 'wishing to please in battle'; 'the bidding in war of' jams two prepositions and loses the stress.

old: "Behold, Arjuna," he said, "the Kurus gathered here."
new: "Look, Arjuna," he said, "at the Kurus gathered here."
why: 1.25 pashya, plain 'look'; 'Behold' is leftover archaism.

old: every one of them a great warrior, mounted on his shining chariot.
new: every one of them a great chariot-warrior.
why: 1.6 sarva eva maharathah, 'all great chariot-fighters'; 'shining' is from Arnold, not the Sanskrit.

old: the mere letter of the scriptures
new: the mere letter of the Vedas
why: Vedas policy. 2.42 vedavadaratah: the text names the Vedas, and the argument of 2.42-46 depends on it.

old: The scriptures deal with the three qualities of nature
new: The Vedas deal with the three qualities of nature
why: Vedas policy. 2.45 traigunyavishaya vedah.

old: the scriptures are worth no more than a well
new: the Vedas are worth no more than a well
why: Vedas policy. 2.46: the well simile is about the Vedas (sarveshu vedeshu).

old: so give yourself to this discipline, for skill in action is exactly this discipline.
new: so give yourself to Yoga, for Yoga is skill in action.
why: Yoga policy. 2.50 yogah karmasu kaushalam, one of the most quoted lines; the inversion and 'discipline' made it unrecognizable.

old: to pass into the peace of God.
new: to reach the nirvana of Brahman.
why: Brahmanirvana policy. 2.72 brahmanirvanam ricchati; 'peace of God' is a Christian phrase and drops both terms.

old: have seen the truth of both — they have learned to tell the abiding substance from the passing shadow.
new: have seen the truth of both.
why: 2.16 ubhayor api drishto 'ntas tv anayos tattvadarshibhih: nothing about substance and shadow; commentary written into the sentence.

old: It is unworthy of you, it shames a brave man, it shuts you out of the noble path.
new: It is unworthy of a noble man; it closes the door to heaven and brings disgrace.
why: 2.2 anaryajushtam asvargyam akirtikaram: unworthy of the noble, not leading to heaven, disgraceful. 'Noble path' put arya in the heaven slot. Arnold: 'it shuts the gate of heaven'.

old: stand up, and be yourself again, scourge of your enemies.
new: stand up, scourge of your enemies.
why: 2.3 uttishtha parantapa; 'be yourself again' is added.

old: Krishna, the lord of hearts;
new: Krishna, the lord of the senses;
why: 2.9 Hrishikesha, 'lord of the senses'; 'hearts' is another epithet.

old: unchanging, present everywhere, steady and sure.
new: unchanging, present everywhere, steady, unmoving, everlasting.
why: 2.24 nityah sarvagatah sthanur acalo 'yam sanatanah; 'sure' drops 'immovable' and 'eternal'.

old: the wisdom of analysis, of Sankhya.
new: the wisdom of Sankhya.
why: Sankhya policy. 2.39 esha te 'bhihita sankhye: keep the name, drop the gloss.

old: But these are not finally two.
why: 3.3-4: Krishna names the two paths and goes straight to 'not by abstaining from action'; their unity is argued at 5.4-5 and is not pre-announced here.

old: Know that action springs from the sacred order itself, and that the sacred, all-pervading, is forever present in every offering.
new: Know that action arises from Brahman, and Brahman from the Imperishable; so Brahman, pervading all things, is forever present in sacrifice.
why: Brahman policy. 3.15 karma brahmodbhavam viddhi brahmakshara-samudbhavam: a two-step chain; the Imperishable was dropped and Brahman blurred to 'the sacred order'.

old: let the wise make such work attractive.
new: let the wise lead them to take joy in all their work.
why: 3.26 joshayet sarvakarmani yuktah samacaran: the wise, working with discipline themselves, should lead the ignorant to delight in their work; 'make attractive' sounds like marketing and loses the example.

old: is fooling no one but himself; he is a hypocrite.
new: is deluded, and he is rightly called a hypocrite.
why: 3.6 vimudhatma mithyacarah sa ucyate.

old: turns his powers to honest work
new: turns his powers of action to the discipline of work
why: 3.7 karmendriyaih karmayogam: the yoga of action with the organs of action; 'honest' moralizes.

old: he is whole, and everything he does is done in the right spirit.
new: he is disciplined, even while he does every kind of work.
why: 4.18 sa yuktah kritsnakarmakrit: he is a yogi and performs all action; 'whole' and 'right spirit' are invented.

old: This undying discipline, this deep union, I once taught to Vivasvat, the lord of light;
new: This undying Yoga I once taught to Vivasvat, the sun;
why: Yoga policy. 4.1 imam vivasvate yogam proktavan aham avyayam: one phrase doubled, and 'lord of light' is a gloss.

old: Now I declare that same ancient discipline to you
new: Now I declare that same ancient Yoga to you
why: Yoga policy. 4.3 sa evayam maya te 'dya yogah proktah puratanah: the teaching named in 4.1 is named again.

old: Age after age I come into the world, in visible form, to protect the good
new: Age after age I am born, to protect the good
why: 4.8 sambhavami yuge yuge; 'in visible form' is added.

old: for the workings of action run deep and dark.
new: for the way of action is hard to fathom.
why: 4.17 gahana karmano gatih; 'and dark' is added for rhythm.

old: knowing me for the one who receives all offering and all worship
new: knowing me for the one who enjoys every sacrifice and every austerity
why: 5.29 bhoktaram yajnatapasam: tapas is austerity, not worship.

old: speak of the way of knowledge and the way of action as two separate things
new: speak of Sankhya and Yoga as two separate things
why: Sankhya/Yoga policy (raised as work-wide pattern, not in 05.md). 5.4 sankhyayogau prithag balah pravadanti: the two schools are named.

old: The state that the followers of knowledge reach is reached by the followers of action as well; whoever sees that the two ways are one sees truly.
new: The state that the followers of Sankhya reach is reached by the followers of Yoga as well; whoever sees that Sankhya and Yoga are one sees truly.
why: Sankhya/Yoga policy. 5.5 yat sankhyaih prapyate sthanam tad yogair api gamyate / ekam sankhyam ca yogam ca yah pashyati sa pashyati.

old: comes to the peace of Brahman, the great extinction. The seers come to that peace,
new: reaches the nirvana of Brahman. The seers win the nirvana of Brahman,
why: Brahmanirvana policy. 5.24-25 brahmanirvanam ... adhigacchati / labhante brahmanirvanam rishayah; 'great' is added. The Sanskrit repeats the term on purpose.

old: the peace of Brahman lies near
new: the nirvana of Brahman lies near
why: Brahmanirvana policy. 5.26 abhito brahmanirvanam vartate.

old: has become one with the eternal.
new: has become Brahman.
why: Brahman policy. 6.27 brahmabhutam.

old: the boundless happiness of touching the eternal.
new: the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman.
why: Brahman policy. 6.28 brahmasamsparsham.

old: lost on the road to the eternal?
new: lost on the road to Brahman?
why: Brahman policy (pattern, not in 06.md). 6.38 vimudho brahmanah pathi.

old: rises beyond the bare word of the scriptures.
new: rises beyond the letter of the Vedas.
why: Vedas policy (pattern, not in 06.md). 6.44 shabdabrahmativartate: the 'word-Brahman' is the Veda.

old: every desire born of his own scheming
new: every desire born of his own imagining
why: 6.24 sankalpaprabhavan kaman: desires born of intention or fancy; 'scheming' adds malice.

old: comes at last to the peace that is the highest of all, the peace that abides in me.
new: comes at last to the peace whose end is nirvana, the peace that abides in me.
why: Brahmanirvana policy. 6.15 shantim nirvanaparamam matsamstham: nirvana was dropped.

old: knowing that all this is the divine, that all this is God.
new: knowing that Vasudeva is all that is.
why: 7.19 vasudevah sarvam iti: the name is the point of the line; the doubled abstraction is filler.

old: the lucid, the passionate, and the dark
new: goodness, passion, and darkness
why: Gunas policy. 7.12 sattvika rajasas tamasah: same English names as XIV and XVII.

old: Earth, water, fire, air, and ether;
new: Earth, water, fire, air, and space;
why: Akasha policy (pattern). 7.4 kham: the same element the edition calls 'space' in IX and now XIII.

old: the sound in the air,
new: the sound in space,
why: Akasha policy (pattern). 7.8 shabdah khe: kha is space, not air (vayu); sound is the quality of space in Sankhya.

old: uttering the single sacred syllable OM — the sound of Brahman — keeps me in mind
new: uttering OM, the single syllable that is Brahman, keeps me in mind
why: 8.13 om ity ekaksharam brahma: OM is Brahman, not its sound.

old: scourge of your enemies — for every offering is made to me.
new: scourge of your enemies.
why: 8.4 adhiyajno 'ham evatra dehe: the dash clause is an added explanation.

old: Among the storm-spirits I am Shankara; among the lords of wealth I am Kubera;
new: Among the Rudras I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas I am Kubera, lord of wealth;
why: 10.23 rudranam shankarash casmi vitteso yaksharakshasam: the Rudras (named in XI) are not the storm-gods (Maruts) of 10.21; the Yakshas and Rakshasas are named, per the named-things policy.

old: Of the chants of the Veda I am the great hymn;
new: Of the Sama chants I am the Brihat Saman;
why: 10.35 brihatsama tatha samnam: a named chant.

old: and I am come forth to annihilate these people.
new: and I have come forth to annihilate these people.
why: 11.32: 'I am come' is leftover archaism in the chapter's most famous line.

old: master of every discipline
new: lord of Yoga
why: Yoga policy. 11.4 yogeshvara.

old: the great lord of all discipline, Krishna,
new: the great lord of Yoga, Krishna,
why: Yoga policy. 11.9 mahayogeshvaro harih.

old: For knowledge is better than blind practice
new: For knowledge is better than practice
why: 12.12 shreyo hi jnanam abhyasat; 'blind' belittles the practice recommended at 12.9-10.

old: who is pure within and capable without, untroubled and unconcerned, who has let go of every anxious undertaking
new: who is pure and capable, untroubled and unconcerned, who has let go of every undertaking
why: 12.16 shucir daksha udasino gatavyathah sarvarambhaparityagi: 'within/without' and 'anxious' are decoration.

old: As the all-pervading air, for its very subtlety, is never tainted by what it moves through,
new: As all-pervading space, for its very subtlety, is never tainted by anything it holds,
why: Akasha policy. 13.32 yatha sarvagatam saukshmyad akasham nopalipyate: akasha is space, not air (vayu); the simile needs what contains all and is untouched.

old: the body as a whole, the power that holds awareness together, and the will to keep on being
new: the body as a whole, awareness, and steadfastness
why: 13.6 sanghatash cetana dhritih: aggregate, consciousness, steadfastness; the paraphrases say what the text does not.

old: the one who knows it — who watches over it — is called
new: the one who knows it is called
why: 13.1 etad yo vetti: 'who watches over it' is a gloss.

old: without the three strands of nature, and yet it experiences them.
new: free of the three qualities of nature, and yet it experiences them.
why: Gunas policy. 13.14 nirgunam gunabhoktri ca.

old: and the three strands they are woven from, are born of nature.
new: and the three qualities, are born of nature.
why: Gunas policy. 13.19 vikarams ca gunams caiva viddhi prakritisambhavan; 'they are woven from' is a gloss.

old: undergoes the strands that nature brings forth; and its clinging to these strands
new: undergoes the qualities that nature brings forth; and its clinging to these qualities
why: Gunas policy. 13.21 bhunkte prakritijan gunan / karanam gunasango 'sya.

old: nature with its three strands
new: nature with its three qualities
why: Gunas policy. 13.23 prakritim ca gunaih saha.

old: others reach it by the discipline of clear reflection,
new: others reach it by the discipline of Sankhya,
why: Sankhya policy. 13.24 anye sankhyena yogena: the school is named.

old: free of the three strands, does not act
new: free of the three qualities, does not act
why: Gunas policy. 13.31 anaditvan nirgunatvat.

old: goodness, passion, and ignorance — are the three qualities
new: goodness, passion, and darkness — are the three qualities
why: Gunas policy. 14.5: tamas is darkness; ignorance is what it is born of (14.8). Naming it 'ignorance' sets up the inversion below and makes 14.16-17 circular.

old: But tamas, born of darkness, deludes
new: But tamas, born of ignorance, deludes
why: 14.8 tamas tv ajnanajam viddhi: tamas is born of ignorance; the edition reversed source and product.

old: the fruit of ignorance is more ignorance still.
new: the fruit of darkness is ignorance.
why: 14.16 ajnanam tamasah phalam: ignorance is the fruit of tamas; the tautology came from the mislabel.

old: gives light and brings health, and it binds
new: gives light, and it binds
why: 14.6 nirmalatvat prakashakam anamayam: 'untroubled' already carries anamayam; 'brings health' doubles it and reads as medical.

old: the divine endowment, the daivi nature.
new: the divine endowment.
why: The untranslated tag gives a reader no help and does not match its partner in seg-0002.

old: the demonic endowment, the asura nature.
new: the demonic endowment.
why: Partner of the seg-0001 fix; 'asura' tag dropped likewise.

old: and a hard, honest discipline of the self; uprightness
new: and austerity; uprightness
why: 16.1 tapa arjavam: austerity, uprightness; 'honest' anticipated arjava, which is then said again.

old: Know them for men whose resolve is set on what is dark.
new: Know them for men of demonic resolve.
why: 17.6 tan viddhy asuranishcayan: demonic resolve; 'dark' files them under tamas and drops the link to XVI.

old: worship the spirits and demons of power;
new: worship the Yakshas and Rakshasas;
why: Named-things policy. 17.4 yaksharakshamsi: named classes of beings; 'of power' is invented. Capitalized as in XI.

old: the priests, the scriptures, and the sacrifices
new: the brahmins, the Vedas, and the sacrifices
why: Vedas policy. 17.23 brahmanas tena vedas ca yajnas ca.

old: words that are true, kind, and to the good
new: words that are true, kind, and helpful
why: 17.15 satyam priyahitam: true, pleasing, beneficial; 'to the good' is not idiomatic.

old: as the teaching of analysis lays them out
new: as the Sankhya teaching lays them out
why: Sankhya policy. 18.13 sankhye kritante.

old: that is the renunciation of light, the only true one.
new: that is the renunciation of light.
why: 18.9 sa tyagah sattviko matah; 'the only true one' is added emphasis.

old: The resolve of light is the unwavering steadiness with which a man holds his mind, his breath, and his senses in hand, fixed in the discipline of devotion.
new: The resolve of light is the steadiness with which a man holds his mind, his breath, and his senses in hand through a discipline that never wavers.
why: 18.33 yogenavyabhicarinya: by unwavering yoga; 'of devotion' narrows it to bhakti, and 'unwavering' belongs to the discipline, not the steadiness.

old: this highest secret, this discipline of devotion, told by Krishna, the lord of all discipline,
new: this highest secret, this Yoga, told by Krishna, the lord of Yoga,
why: Yoga policy. 18.75 guhyam etat param yogam yogeshvarat krishnat: 'of devotion' narrows it to bhakti.

old: Wherever Krishna is, the lord of all discipline,
new: Wherever Krishna is, the lord of Yoga,
why: Yoga policy. 18.78 yatra yogeshvarah krishnah; Arnold too: 'Lord of Yoga'.

old: and faith in things unseen
new: and religious faith
why: 18.42 astikyam: belief in the sacred teaching; 'things unseen' echoes Hebrews 11:1.
